meta.host: AMD EPYC 9754, shared host, cores 128-223 without SMT siblings: milestone m1029-mqcd's G1 on 2026-10-29 (17:21-19:07 UTC), at most one job per CCX of 8 cores, each on the least busy core of a CCX whose least busy core was below 50 % busy (cores per record: host_cpus); host load average 52-247 (other users' processes and the milestone's whole-suite gate ran at the same time); timings indicative (user 2026-10-28), one round, no repeats for contention

main_rule.rule: every cell shows the most recent configuration that measured it; A is newer than B if B's revision is an ancestor of A's (git merge-base --is-ancestor, recorded in milestone.json ancestry) or if A is the development side and B the integrated side of one G1 campaign, transitively; equal revisions keep the order development, integrated, development_records; the registry (no run) comes last; without a measurement, the status of the newest configuration with a record of the row
main_rule.validation_rule: a newer comparison with fewer points or fewer references than an older one and no larger deviation repeats part of it: the older, more complete comparison stays in the cell and the repeat is listed in partial_repeats; a newer comparison with a larger deviation, or at least as many points and every reference, replaces it
main_rule.generation_rule: a generation multiplier pairs values timed under the same kind of conditions: in a G1 row the campaign's provider generation with a G1 configuration; a newer development record there (shared host under load) has no multiplier; in the other rows the development record with the providers' reference runs, both run records on this shared host outside the G1 protocol
main_rule.source: scripts/build_summary.py MAIN_RULE, VALIDATION_RULE, GENERATION_RULE, Recency; ancestry: milestone.json ancestry

gate_decisions.what: user verdicts: decisions replace a measured open (inconclusive) gate verdict of their process and batch; threshold_rule removes the blocking gate below 5 ms per point; the measured ratio and band stay as measured

decisions.label: user decision 2026-10-24
decisions.reason: parity within the band (1.00 of the limit, band 0.90-1.10, after the single repeat of plan 5.8) is judged a pass
decisions.status: no longer applies: the G1 re-measure on loop (4e9b5a9e, native inputs) is a measured pass at B = 128 after its single repeat (0.87 of the limit, band 0.78-0.95); a decision applies to a measured open verdict of its process and batch only

threshold_rule.label: below 5 ms: not gated (user 2026-10-24)
threshold_rule.applies: a process whose pyAmpliCol time per point at B = 128 is below 5 ms has no blocking gate: its ratio and band stay as measured and are shown, its verdict is the label; the batched time is the configuration's own at B = 128 (the gate batch, user 2026-10-28: every other batch size, B = 1 and the 2->5 rows' B = 16 included, is reported with its ratio and band and carries no verdict; a configuration without a B = 128 timing, e.g. the one-lane runs, has none, never one derived from another batch size); it takes precedence over a decision; the exact-rational vs binary64 input question is therefore moot and the protocol stays
threshold_rule.source: workspace/reports/engine-v2/slice-status.md, DECISIONS, 2026-10-24 ~22:35 UTC (USER: summary pages and gate focus, GATE RULE; binding for the milestone push's report:gint and for gate verdicts)

validation_decisions.what: user acceptances of the points where a validation check exceeds its tolerance: the check, its tolerance and its passed: false stay as measured (never widened); the accepted points are marked and shown with the label instead of a failure. scripts/build_summary.py (_accepted) requires the accepted points to be exactly the check's points above the tolerance, each within pyAmpliCol's binary64 estimate E there and with pyAmpliCol's double-double value on the shown reference within the tolerance, and stops otherwise
